passage: Tejas, put the phone down and listen. I'm Vinita, and I want to tell you about the hair clips. When I was ten, a man I barely knew, older than my father, stopped me near the bus stop and gave me a pretty set of clips. "Our little secret, no need to tell your parents," he said. I liked the clips, but my stomach felt wrong, and the word secret sat on me like a stone. That evening I put them on the table and told my mother everything. She held my hand and said, "You did the right thing. None of this is your fault." That same evening my father called the school. I stayed away from that bus stop. Never blame yourself, Tejas. Telling is always right.

qa.q: What did the man give Vinita?
How did Vinita feel about the secret even though she liked the clips?
qa.a: Vinita felt uneasy and worried: her stomach felt wrong and the word secret sat on her like a stone, so a gift with a secret felt like a warning.

qa.q: What should Tejas do if an older person gives Tejas presents and says to keep it secret?
qa.a: Tell their parents right away and stay away from that person.

qa.q: How might Vinita's mother have felt when Vinita told her?
qa.a: Grateful and protective, since she held Vinita's hand, said it was not Vinita's fault, and the school was told that same evening.

grounding: An elder recalls an older stranger giving presents and asking for secrecy, and how telling their parents right away and staying away was right and not their fault.

passage: Last month, a man I didn't know started waiting near the gate of my tuition class. First he gave me a chocolate, then a keychain. On Thursday he held out a toy car for my little brother Mohit and said, 'This is our secret, Seema. Don't tell your parents.' My stomach went cold. A present with a secret felt wrong, like a trap. I took Mohit's hand and walked straight home without the toy. I told Mummy everything, even about the chocolate I had already eaten. I thought she would be cross. She hugged me and said, 'You did nothing wrong. Telling me was exactly right.' That evening Papa and Mummy went with me to the tuition teacher and then to the police station near our colony. Now Papa picks us up every day.

qa.q: Where did the man start waiting?
qa.a: Near the gate of Seema's tuition class.

qa.q: What does Seema's cold stomach suggest about how the secret felt?
qa.a: Seema felt scared and uneasy; a present tied to a secret felt wrong, like a trap.

qa.q: Which choices kept Seema and Mohit safe?
qa.a: Refusing the toy, walking straight home and telling Mummy everything the same day; the parents then told the tuition teacher and the police that evening.

qa.q: How might Mummy have felt when Seema told her?
qa.a: Worried, but relieved and proud that Seema spoke up; she hugged Seema and said telling was exactly right.

grounding: A child is given presents by an unknown man who asks for secrecy, recognises the warning, and tells a parent at once, who acts the same evening.

passage:
Incident note, Friday, by Ms Maria, Class 4 teacher.
During pickup, I saw an older man at the side gate hand Varun a small wrapped box. Varun took a step back and did not open it. When his father arrived a minute later, Varun ran to him and said, loud enough for me to hear, 'Papa, that man gave me presents three times. He said it's our secret.' Varun's hands were trembling, but he kept talking. His father knelt and told him he was right to tell. I stayed with them and told Varun it was never his fault. Within half an hour I had reported it to our safeguarding lead, who called the police and alerted the guards. Varun went home holding his father's hand.

qa.q: What did the man at the side gate hand Varun?
What was Varun feeling when he told his father, and how can you tell?
qa.a: He was frightened but brave; his hands were trembling, yet he kept talking.

qa.q: What did the adults do right after Varun spoke up?
qa.a: His father said he was right to tell, Ms Maria said it was never his fault, and she reported it to the safeguarding lead within half an hour.

qa.q: How might Varun's father have felt hearing about the secret presents?
qa.a: Shocked and worried, but he knelt and reassured Varun instead of blaming him.

grounding: A teacher's note records a boy telling his father about secret gifts from an older stranger and the same-day steps adults took.
